episodes.214445: A cluster of slow moving thunderstorms with very heavy rain moved over Fort Peck Lake and the surrounding areas in the early morning hours.
episodes.214465: A strong upper level high was centered over east-central NM July 29th shifting a little west to central NM by July 30th. Daytime heating and moisture under the high resulted in thunderstorm development across the higher terrain midday both days. Thunderstorms over the Sangre de Cristo Mountains moved east-southeast into the adjacent highlands and plains over far northeast NM during the afternoon and evening hours with one storm producing a 63 mph wind gust at Raton Crews Airport on July 29th and another storm producing a 59 mph wind gust at Clayton Municipal Airport on July 30th. Thunderstorms tapered off during the evening hours with the loss of daytime heating.
episodes.214824: Hot summer weather prevailed at the end of July with scattered afternoon and evening storms, some of which were severe.  In addition, extreme heat prevailed on July 28-29 with peak heat index values of 113F or higher.
episodes.215829: A weak trough of low pressure developed around the Coastal Plain of Eastern North Carolina during the late afternoon and evening hours of July twenty-nineth. Out ahead and along this trough, isolated to widely scattered clusters of thunderstorms developed a few of which became strong in nature as they tracked southeastwards across portions of the inner rivers and sounds of Eastern North Carolina. The strongest storm brought strong wind gusts to portions of the Pamlico Sound just past midnight on July Thirtieth.
episodes.215933: A few rounds of thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the coast and the adjacent coastal waters. The first cluster of thunderstorms impacted the southeast Georgia coast and the nearby Atlantic coastal waters with strong wind gusts in the afternoon hours. Then late in the evening, another cluster of storms impacted the southeast South Carolina coast.
episodes.215934: A cluster of thunderstorms developed in the late evening hours and moved through the North Charleston and Charleston metro areas. The storms produced damaging wind gusts and one report of hail.
episodes.215951: A weakening frontal boundary over southeast Georgia shifted southward and stalled along the I-10 corridor on the afternoon of July 30th. An unstable airmass, high moisture (PWATs 2+ inches) and lift from the stalled front enhanced wet microburst activity and localized flooding. On July 31st, similar setup as July 30th but with some drier air in the area aiding in isolated downburst development.
episodes.216088: Thunderstorms developed during the early afternoon hours of July 30 along the Cherry County and South Dakota border. As this activity tracked to the southeast, it morphed into a line of severe thunderstorms. As the afternoon progressed, a line of storms extended from south central Cherry County into western Boyd and northwestern Holt counties. This line tracked southeast into central Nebraska clearing Custer and eastern Lincoln County by 9 PM CDT. Thunderstorm wind gusts to 80 MPH were reported Near Brownlee along with flash flooding in Valentine. Hail up to ping pong ball size was reported in Stapleton.
episodes.216110: A prolific monsoon pattern continued to end July, resulting in additional instances of thunderstorm wind gusts and flash flooding. Additionally, an active wildfire resulted in the development of a brief fire tornado.
episodes.216117: Another round of monsoon thunderstorms forms during the afternoon hours.  A couple of the storms reach severe levels and the heavy rain led to areas of flash flooding.
episodes.216423: An isolated strong thunderstorm produced high wind near the town of Hayes in central South Dakota, with peak wind gusts of 65 and 63 mph measured on personal weather stations.
episodes.216424: Storms produced heavy rainfall on July 30th into the early morning of July 31st, with a number of reports of rainfall at or in excess of 5 inches centered across Day and Roberts counties. Heavy rainfall resulted in flooding and stalled cars in the city of Aberdeen with the Official National Weather Service observation of 2.55 inches. Flooding also impacted the cities of Pierre and Fort Pierre including portions of US Highway 14. Multiple roads and county/state highways were closed north of US Highway 12 in Day county due to water over the road, including Highway 33 near Roslyn and Highway 27 near Pierpont. The highest reported measured total was 6.90 inches by the CoCoRaHS observer 6.6 miles east northeast of Grenville (Day County).||There was also a brief period of minor flooding along the Little Minnesota River near Peever, after 5.8 inches was recorded by the COOP observer in Sisseton, and 6.34 was measured by the CoCoRaHS observer 10 miles east northeast of Sisseton.
episodes.216495: Another subtle wave in the broader flow, coupled with moisture in place, allowed for strong storms to develop across the Wet Mountain Valley and Wet Mountains.
episodes.216528: There was enough monsoonal moisture to develop isolated thunderstorms in Southwest MT. A hot and dry surface layer allowed for an isolated severe wind gust to develop.
episodes.216735: Showers and thunderstorms developed early in the morning over parts of central north Dakota. A stronger thunderstorm formed and produced a wind gust of 60 mph at the NDAWN station in Hurdsfield.
episodes.216859: An area of low pressure east of the region retrograded back to the west toward the Hudson Valley and Catskills during the afternoon and evening of the 29th, resulting in bands of scattered showers and thunderstorms, especially across Central NY. Showers and storms began to train over the same area leading to locally heavy rainfall and urban flash flooding in portions of Broome County.
episodes.216964: Clusters of thunderstorms produced large swaths of damaging winds across much of western SD.
episodes.216966: Two rounds of severe weather impacted the region the last two days of July.
episodes.217059: Severe thunderstorms produced damaging winds over parts of Eastern ND. Some of the slower moving thunderstorms resulted in localized street flooding in the Grand Forks, ND metro area.
episodes.217179: Thunderstorms produced strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.217187: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced strong winds.
episodes.217217: Thunderstorms developed across southwest Alabama and produced gusty winds.
